title: Cyber-eval reciprocity attestation lands as agent-registry GA default by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 the Indo-Pacific cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema — first wired into the Sunday three-hyperscaler registry interop matrix as a tenant-policy field set, then carried into Tuesday's OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise per-org agent registry GA cohort for Singapore-cloud and Japan-cloud tenants on Microsoft Azure plus AWS Bedrock plus Google Cloud Vertex simultaneously — becomes the de facto cross-vendor agent-registry GA-tier tenant-policy default across the four-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix (OpenAI Codex CLI plus Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Microsoft Azure AI Foundry plus Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center). The trigger is the simultaneous Tuesday landing of three structurally complementary moves: the Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter crosses to eleven named jurisdictions with the first formal Latin American extension (Thailand entry note plus Chile and Mexico exploratory observers under the OECD GENAI working-group baseline), giving the schema cross-hemispheric reach; OpenAI cites the May 8 Singapore IMDA plus Japan AISI memorandum plus the Sunday-shipped South Korea PIPC plus New Zealand GCSB reciprocity-attestation fields as the operative tenant-policy schema for the per-org agent registry GA cohort, anchoring the schema at the hyperscaler agent-registry GA tier rather than the public-preview tier; and the four-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix completes in pre-GA form with Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center managed interop joining the Codex CLI plus Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Azure AI Foundry pre-GA cohort, demonstrating that the reciprocity-attestation field schema is the only tenant-policy primitive every vendor in the matrix already speaks. The structural force is procurement-driven rather than standards-driven: when the schema is the only cross-vendor primitive shared across a four-vendor interop matrix AND the hyperscaler GA-tier tenant-policy schema AND the eleven-jurisdiction allied policy regime AND the Tuesday Verifiable Cross-Hemispheric Composition arxiv 2605.06584 paper as the citable formal-verification anchor, the cohort-completion gravity locks the schema as the default at the agent-registry GA tier — any vendor shipping a GA registry on a hyperscaler sovereign-cloud tenancy without the attestation fields fails procurement gating from the Indo-Pacific cohort. The landing shape: by Q3 2026 at least one additional frontier-lab agent registry (Mistral or Anthropic) ships GA on the same Singapore plus Japan sovereign-cloud tenancy citing the same reciprocity-attestation field schema, and at least one hyperscaler publishes a Skill Catalog or Agent Governance Center GA tier requiring the attestation fields as the default tenant-policy schema for new agent-registry provisioning on Indo-Pacific sovereign-cloud regions. The US recognition gap remains the structural pressure point — the schema lands as a cross-vendor GA default regardless of whether the FMRB executive order signs first, because the procurement-enforcement pathway is already cross-vendor and cross-hyperscaler on the eleven-jurisdiction perimeter. Bear case is that the FMRB executive order ships a US-side mandatory schema variant that fragments the field set before the cross-vendor GA default locks; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the schema as the operative agent-registry GA tenant-policy default across the four-vendor matrix on Indo-Pacific sovereign-cloud tenants.

reasoning.because: Tuesday OpenAI per-org agent registry GA cites reciprocity-attestation fields as tenant schema.
reasoning.given: It is the only cross-vendor primitive shared by the four-vendor matrix and 11-jurisdiction cohort.
reasoning.so_that: At least one more frontier-lab registry + one hyperscaler Skill Catalog ship GA defaulting to the schema.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; Indo-Pacific sovereign-cloud tenants; agent-registry GA tier.
reasoning.plain_language: Allied countries agreed on a list of AI safety checks; vendors now use it for enterprise setups, and it will be the default by autumn.

summary: OpenAI's Tuesday per-org agent registry GA on Singapore and Japan sovereign-cloud cites the Indo-Pacific reciprocity-attestation fields as the tenant-policy schema; the four-vendor interop matrix shares no other primitive. By Q3 2026 the schema becomes the cross-vendor agent-registry GA default.
